brief.problem_statement: Determine the optimal segment mix, loan pricing, approval policy, and launch plan for FinNova Capital's 1-year small-business loan pilot to maximize risk-adjusted financial returns amid a severe credit-risk spike.
supplied_facts: FinNova Capital is launching a 1-year small-business loan pilot.
Retail shop default rate increased to 8.0%.
Service SME default rate increased to 5.0%.
Small manufacturer default rate increased to 7.0%.
The risk committee requires overall portfolio default to remain <= 5.5%.
The risk committee requires maintaining a minimum liquid reserve of INR 3 crore.
identified_assumptions: [ASSUMPTION: Market demand in the lower-risk Service SME segment is high enough to absorb a higher portfolio allocation.]
[ASSUMPTION: Total available lending capital is fixed for the 1-year pilot duration.]
[ASSUMPTION: Customer acquisition costs and operational overhead per segment remain constant despite pricing and policy shifts.]
[ASSUMPTION: Pricing adjustments will not significantly degrade borrower conversion rates in affected segments.]
hard_constraints: Overall portfolio default rate must be <= 5.5%.
Minimum liquid reserve of INR 3 crore must be maintained.
Time horizon is strictly limited to a 1-year pilot.
success_criteria: Maximize risk-adjusted financial returns for the 1-year pilot.
Maintain regulatory, risk committee, and capital compliance (default rate <= 5.5%, reserve >= INR 3 crore).
Define a finalized optimal segment mix, loan pricing strategy, approval policy, and operational launch plan.

Business Research.summary: FinNova Capital's 1-year small-business loan pilot must strategically pivot capital toward lower-risk segments like Service SMEs (5.0% default) to offset credit spikes in Retail (8.0%) and Manufacturing (7.0%) while adhering to the 5.5% portfolio default cap and maintaining a minimum liquid reserve of INR 3 crore.
key_findings: Severe credit-risk divergence exists across segments: Retail shops demonstrate the highest default rate at 8.0%, followed by Small Manufacturers at 7.0% and Service SMEs at 5.0%.
To satisfy the risk committee's mandate of an overall portfolio default rate <= 5.5%, capital allocation must be heavily weighted toward the lower-risk Service SME segment.
Operations and loan deployment are bounded by a mandatory minimum liquid reserve of INR 3 crore and a fixed 1-year pilot time horizon.
recommendations: Over-index portfolio mix toward Service SMEs to keep baseline risk within the <= 5.5% default requirement.
Re-evaluate pricing structures and tighten approval policies for Retail and Manufacturing segments to compensate for 8.0% and 7.0% default rates.
Establish continuous capital tracking to prevent liquidity from dropping below the mandatory INR 3 crore reserve.
Business Research.financial_or_operational_impact: High financial optimization potential by rebalancing portfolio capital toward Service SMEs, constrained by a strict 5.5% default ceiling and an INR 3 crore reserve requirement.
explicit_assumptions: [ASSUMPTION: Market demand in the lower-risk Service SME segment is high enough to absorb a higher portfolio allocation.]
[ASSUMPTION: Total available lending capital is fixed for the 1-year pilot duration.]
[ASSUMPTION: Customer acquisition costs and operational overhead per segment remain constant despite pricing and policy shifts.]
[ASSUMPTION: Pricing adjustments will not significantly degrade borrower conversion rates in affected segments.]
[ASSUMPTION: The addressable market for small-business lending will remain stable despite sector-wide credit risk spikes.]

Marketing & Sales.summary: Aggressively scale acquisition within the lower-risk Service SME segment via targeted B2B digital performance marketing and accounting software partnerships to build portfolio volume while staying under the strict 5.5% default cap. High-risk segments like Retail (8.0% default) and Manufacturing (7.0% default) will be funnel-gated via stringent top-of-funnel pre-qualification and risk-adjusted pricing.
key_findings: Service SMEs present the lowest credit risk profile (5.0% default rate), making them the ideal Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) for aggressive volume scaling under the 5.5% portfolio default limit.
Broad-reach advertising for Retail (8.0% default) and Manufacturing (7.0% default) yields high customer acquisition costs (CAC) due to high top-of-funnel drop-off from mandatory risk gating.
B2B FinTech and accounting integrations offer high-intent, lower-CAC acquisition pipelines compared to unsegmented digital channels.
recommendations: Allocate 70% of direct marketing spend toward Service SMEs via LinkedIn B2B targeted ads, Google Search (high-intent loan queries), and industry associations.
Form revenue-share acquisition partnerships with SME cloud-accounting platforms (e.g., Zoho, Tally) to source pre-vetted financial profiles at a fixed CAC.

Deploy a tiered GTM rollout: Phase 1 focuses exclusively on high-margin Service SMEs; Phase 2 introduces selective, risk-adjusted pricing packages for premium, low-risk sub-segments of Small Manufacturers.
Marketing & Sales.financial_or_operational_impact: Requires an initial marketing acquisition budget of INR 45 Lakhs; projects acquiring 350+ funded SME accounts in H1 while maintaining an average CAC under INR 12,500 per funded loan.
explicit_assumptions: [ASSUMPTION: Paid search conversion rate from ad click to completed loan application is 3.8%.]
[ASSUMPTION: Service SME application-to-approval conversion rate is 22.0% under modified risk policy.]
[ASSUMPTION: Accounting software partnership channels will yield a funded loan conversion rate of 12.0%.]
